datasets.legal_basis: Health and Social Care Act 2012 – s261(2)(a)
datasets.name: Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS)

states.expected_benefits:
The findings of this analysis will be entered into the Inquiry’s evidence and will enable a robust, statistically-grounded understanding of patterns of inpatient deaths and contributing factors. 

Measurable public-benefit outcomes include: 
•	Evidence-based recommendations to reduce future avoidable deaths and improve patient-safety systems within mental-health inpatient care;
•	Identification of systemic issues in care, governance and escalation pathways across NHS trusts;
•	Improvements in data-quality and transparency, supporting NHSE’s wider learning-from-deaths programme; and
•	Transferable learning to other regions and services beyond Essex, supporting national policy on mental-health safety. 

These benefits are directly aligned with the Inquiry’s statutory Terms of Reference and deliver tangible improvements to health-system governance and patient outcomes.
states.expected_output:
The Inquiry’s Expert Health Statisticians will publish a report containing the findings of their analysis. This report will be entered into the Inquiry’s evidence and will be made publicly available via the Lampard Inquiry website. The Inquiry might also reference these findings in their final report. 

The outputs will not contain NHS England Data and will only contain aggregated information with small numbers suppressed as appropriate in line with the relevant disclosure rules for the dataset(s) from which the information was derived.

•	The outputs will be communicated to relevant recipients through the following dissemination channels
•	Disclosure to Core Participants under confidentiality undertaking
•	Public report, published on the Inquiry’s website
•	Public Inquiry hearings
states.objective:
The Data will be used for the purpose of supporting the Lampard Inquiry, which is a statutory investigation into mental health inpatient deaths in Essex between 2000 and 2023. It is led by Baroness Kate Lampard CBE and builds on the work of the Essex Mental Health Independent Inquiry.

The Data will be processed in line with The Lampard Inquiry’s Terms of Reference (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/lampard-inquiry-terms-of-reference/terms-of-reference-for-the-lampard-inquiry) which includes (but is not limited to):

The investigation of the deaths of which the inquiry will consider:
•	serious failings related to the delivery of safe and therapeutic inpatient treatment and care, which may include consideration of circumstances where serious harm short of death occurred
•	how and the extent to which patients were engaged with and involved in decisions in relation to their care
•	how and the extent to which families, carers or other members of a patient’s support network were engaged with and involved in decisions in relation to the patient’s care, including any engagement after the patient’s death
•	matters relating to physical and sexual safety within mental health inpatient units at the trusts
•	the actions, practices and behaviours of permanent, temporary and agency staff providing mental health inpatient care at the trusts
•	the approach to staffing, training and working conditions of permanent, temporary and agency staff providing mental health inpatient care at the trusts; including the support provided to and the supervision of such staff
•	the actions, practices and behaviours of leadership in relation to mental health inpatient care at the trusts
•	the culture and the wider governance of and at the trusts
•	the quality of investigations undertaken or commissioned by the trusts in relation to mental health inpatient care

Following a formal notice of conversion issued by the Department of Health and Social Care on 27 October 2023, the Inquiry was granted statutory status, giving it legal powers to compel evidence and witness participation. 

This Data Sharing Agreement permits access to Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS) for the purposes of the Lampard Inquiry.

This Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) covers the provision of the environment within the Secure Data Environment in which experts appointed by the Lampard Inquiry will access data for the purpose of producing a report to support the Lampard Inquiry with the following ongoing investigations:
-	Identification and analysis of serious failings in the delivery of care and therapeutic inpatient treatment and care
-	Supporting examination of the actions, practices, and behaviours of staff involved in mental health inpatient care. 
-	Contributing to the assessment of the culture and governance within NHS trusts and its impact on care and treatment outcomes. 
-	Facilitating review of the quality and adequacy of investigations and responses by NHS trusts and other relevant bodies. 
-	Supporting scrutiny of interactions between NHS trusts and other public bodies, including commissioners, coroners, professional regulators and the Care Quality Commission.
